About: Pool cleaning and repair. Advertises itself as Voted Best of Tracy, which means they enter and promote local competitions. Central Valley heat makes pool service a near-necessity, and the buyer is a homeowner with a pool - a supermarket regular.
Notes: PRIORITY 2. Already advertises a Best of Tracy win, so they buy local visibility. Get the owner name.

About: Over 20 years in business, open daily 8:30-5. The business name itself is a price claim. Separate category from Automotive Repair, so this fills a slot rather than competing with the six auto shops already on the list.
Notes: PRIORITY 2. Distinct category from the auto repair leads, so no exclusivity conflict. Price-led marketing means they already advertise.

About: Mobile only, comes to the home or office at no extra fee. 86 reviews, Mon-Sat. ANGLE: no storefront means zero passing trade, so every customer has to be reached by advertising. That is the strongest structural case for a cart panel of any lead found. CAUTION: mobile operators are usually small, so expect the lowest-cost panel.
Notes: PRIORITY 3. Backup to Lowest Price Auto Glass - only one auto glass slot exists, so do not book both.

About: Jon Highland is the owner; artist Kristal also named. Has its own site. Scarcity is unusually real and easy to prove. Tattoo work is discretionary and highly visual, which suits a full-colour panel far better than text search.
Notes: PRIORITY 3. Save Mart-only category and this is a Save Mart - genuinely exclusive slot. Owner name already known: Jon Highland.

About: Three tattooists with a combined 20+ years. Notes: PRIORITY 4. Backup for the tattoo slot. VERIFY the phone number first - it may belong to Art Official Studios.

About: Walk-ins welcome. Specialises in black and grey realism, portraits, colour and traditional. Listed as open 24 hours, which is likely a directory error worth confirming. ANGLE: walk-in trade is impulse trade, which is what a cart panel drives. GAP: no owner name and no confirmed address.

About: Gymnastics and parkour for all ages, including a Parent Tot class for walking to three years. On N Tracy Blvd, the same road as the store. About: Fine art family portraits, maternity and newborn, senior portraits, pets, executive, weddings, plus custom framing. 87 photos and ~24 reviews. Being the studio they already recognise is the whole game. Custom framing is a second visit from the same customer.
Notes: PRIORITY 1. Life-event purchase from exactly the cart audience. Downtown, so they need reach they do not get from Tracy Blvd traffic.

About: Dance studio since 1995. 3,800 sq ft with three rooms, more than 250 dancers aged 2 to 18. ANGLE: 250 enrolled dancers means 250 paying families, and 30 years in town means they grow by word of mouth among parents. A separate slot from Fitness and Gymnastics, so booking them does not block a gymnastics sale. Chamber membership signals they invest in local presence.
Notes: PRIORITY 2. Distinct category from gymnastics - both slots can be sold. 30 years and 250 families. Get the owner name.

About: Over 16 years in Tracy. Competitive gymnastics, Ninja Zone for boys, and tumbling for dancers and cheerleaders. 56 reviews. Same building complex as D2M Dance, so one trip covers two appointments in two different categories.
Notes: PRIORITY 2. Backup for the gymnastics slot behind Royal, but stack the trip with D2M - same complex at 3602 Mars.

Notes: PRIORITY 2. On N Tracy Blvd. Gold buying plus gift seasonality. Get the owner name - the Ybarra family presumably.

CAUTION: also covers Livermore, so ask whether Tracy alone is worth it to him.
Notes: PRIORITY 2. Owner name already known: Scott LaPlante, founder since 1988. Certified arborist is a real differentiator.

Notes: PRIORITY 3. Life-event purchase that overlaps the realtor and attorney audiences. Get the on-site manager name.

About: Pawn loans and gold buying. Open Tue-Fri 10-6, Sat 11-5, closed Sun and Mon.
